statement: A jacket has a price tag of $\$80$. The store takes $25\%$ off the tag price, and then Omar uses a coupon that takes $10\%$ off the sale price. How many dollars does Omar pay?

choices.misconception: I took 25% off to get 60, then took 10 dollars off instead of 10 percent, so 60 - 10 = 50.
I added the two discounts to get 35% off the tag price, and 65% of 80 is 52.
I took 25% off the tag price but forgot to use the coupon, so I stopped at 60.
I used only the 10% coupon on the 80 dollar tag and forgot the 25% sale.

hints: Do the two discounts one after the other, not together.
First find the sale price. Then take $10\%$ of the sale price, not of $\$80$.
The sale price is $80 - 20 = 60$ dollars. Ten percent of $60$ is $6$.

solutions.reliable: Twenty-five percent of $\$80$ is $\$20$, so the sale price is $\$60$. Ten percent of $\$60$ is $\$6$, so Omar pays $60 - 6 = 54$ dollars.
solutions.elegant: Each discount multiplies the price: $80 \cdot 0.75 \cdot 0.9 = 60 \cdot 0.9 = 54$. The coupon works on a smaller price, which is why the total discount is less than $35\%$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
